Drought and wet events of an index series.

Source: R/index_events.R
Index-events.Rd

index_events finds the drought (or wet) events of a series of a drought index, such as the SPEI or the SPI, and returns their start, end, duration, severity, intensity and peak, using the run theory of Yevjevich (1967).

Usage

index_events(x, type = "dry", threshold = NULL, min.duration = 1, pool = 0)

Arguments

x

the index values: an object of class spei (as returned by spei or spi), whose fitted values are used; a univariate or multivariate time series (ts); a numeric vector; or a numeric matrix with one column per series. Three-dimensional arrays (gridded data) are not supported (see 'Details').

type

the type of events, either 'dry' (default) or 'wet'.

threshold

the threshold that defines an event. A dry event is a run of consecutive time steps with the index at or below the threshold, and a wet event a run with the index at or above it. Defaults to -1 for dry events and to 1 for wet events.

min.duration

a positive integer, the minimum duration (number of time steps) of an event. Shorter events are discarded. Defaults to 1 (all events are kept).

pool

a non-negative integer. Events separated by pool time steps or fewer are merged into one event (pooling). Defaults to 0 (no pooling).

Value

A data frame with one row per event, in chronological order (and by series, if there are several), with the columns:

  • site: only if x has several series (columns), the series of the event: its column name, or its column number if the columns have no names.

  • start, end: the first and the last time step of the event.

  • duration: the number of time steps of the event.

  • severity: the sum of the index values over the event.

  • intensity: the severity divided by the duration.

  • peak: the most extreme index value of the event.

  • peak.time: the time step of the peak (the first one, if it is reached more than once).

If x is a time series with a whole-number frequency, the time steps (start, end and peak.time) are labels: 'YYYY-MM' for monthly series (e.g. '2011-03'), 'YYYY' for annual series, and 'YYYY-Pnn' for other frequencies, with the period nn within the year (e.g. '1961-P05' for the fifth period of 1961). For time series with other frequencies they are the decimal times given by time. If x carries no time information (a vector or a matrix), they are the positions of the time steps in the series. If there are no events, the data frame has no rows.

Details

Following the run theory (Yevjevich, 1967), an event is a run of consecutive time steps in which the index is beyond a threshold: at or below threshold for dry events, at or above it for wet events. The run starts at the first time step beyond the threshold and ends at the last one.

A missing value (NA) breaks an event: the time steps before and after it belong to different events. Missing values at the start of the series (the first scale - 1 time steps of the SPEI or the SPI at time scale scale) are simply skipped.

With pool greater than 0, two consecutive events separated by pool or fewer time steps are merged into one event, which spans from the start of the first one to the end of the second one. The time steps between them count in the duration of the merged event, and their values in its severity. Events separated by a missing value are never merged. min.duration is applied after pooling.

The severity of an event is the sum of the index values over its time steps, so it is negative for dry events (with a negative threshold) and positive for wet events. Its intensity is the severity divided by the duration (the mean value of the index during the event), and its peak is the most extreme value of the index: the lowest one for dry events and the highest one for wet events. Note that other definitions of severity are used in the literature, such as the cumulative deficit below the threshold; it can be computed from the output as threshold * duration - severity for dry events.

The function works on series. To get the events of each cell of gridded data (a 3-d array), apply it to the series of each cell, e.g. index_events(x[, i, j]).

References

Yevjevich, V. 1967. An objective approach to definitions and investigations of continental hydrologic droughts. Hydrology Paper 23, Colorado State University, Fort Collins.

See also

spei, spi.

Examples

# SPEI-12 at Wichita
data(wichita)
wichita$PET <- thornthwaite(wichita$TMED, 37.6475, verbose = FALSE)
wichita$BAL <- wichita$PRCP - wichita$PET
wichita <- ts(wichita[, -c(1, 2)], end = c(2011, 10), frequency = 12)
spei12 <- spei(wichita[, "BAL"], 12, verbose = FALSE)

# Drought events (SPEI-12 at or below -1)
index_events(spei12)
#>      start     end duration   severity intensity      peak peak.time
#> 1  1980-12 1981-09       10 -16.317124 -1.631712 -1.916626   1981-04
#> 2  1985-04 1985-05        2  -2.397704 -1.198852 -1.232911   1985-05
#> 3  1988-08 1989-06       11 -17.732251 -1.612023 -1.884387   1989-04
#> 4  1990-08 1992-01       18 -27.378900 -1.521050 -1.865432   1991-03
#> 5  1994-05 1994-11        7  -8.428643 -1.204092 -1.356032   1994-06
#> 6  1996-06 1996-08        3  -3.132460 -1.044153 -1.060782   1996-06
#> 7  2001-07 2001-07        1  -1.164280 -1.164280 -1.164280   2001-07
#> 8  2001-11 2002-06        8 -10.523032 -1.315379 -1.536284   2002-03
#> 9  2010-11 2010-11        1  -1.023504 -1.023504 -1.023504   2010-11
#> 10 2011-05 2011-10        6  -9.628277 -1.604713 -1.808277   2011-09

# Only those lasting six months or more, merging events separated by one
# or two months
index_events(spei12, min.duration = 6, pool = 2)
#>     start     end duration   severity intensity      peak peak.time
#> 1 1980-12 1981-09       10 -16.317124 -1.631712 -1.916626   1981-04
#> 2 1988-08 1989-06       11 -17.732251 -1.612023 -1.884387   1989-04
#> 3 1990-08 1992-01       18 -27.378900 -1.521050 -1.865432   1991-03
#> 4 1994-05 1994-11        7  -8.428643 -1.204092 -1.356032   1994-06
#> 5 2001-11 2002-06        8 -10.523032 -1.315379 -1.536284   2002-03
#> 6 2011-05 2011-10        6  -9.628277 -1.604713 -1.808277   2011-09

# Wet events (SPEI-12 at or above 1)
index_events(spei12, type = "wet")
#>      start     end duration  severity intensity     peak peak.time
#> 1  1987-08 1987-08        1  1.009934  1.009934 1.009934   1987-08
#> 2  1993-02 1993-02        1  1.066617  1.066617 1.066617   1993-02
#> 3  1993-05 1993-10        6  7.859985  1.309998 1.817992   1993-05
#> 4  1995-06 1995-06        1  1.108589  1.108589 1.108589   1995-06
#> 5  1995-08 1995-09        2  2.344999  1.172500 1.179370   1995-08
#> 6  1998-01 1998-01        1  1.038569  1.038569 1.038569   1998-01
#> 7  1998-03 1998-04        2  2.217452  1.108726 1.172832   1998-03
#> 8  1999-06 2000-07       14 21.163668  1.511691 2.053076   2000-03
#> 9  2004-07 2004-08        2  2.593585  1.296793 1.451115   2004-07
#> 10 2008-05 2009-08       16 32.505565  2.031598 2.905221   2009-04
#> 11 2009-10 2009-10        1  1.061464  1.061464 1.061464   2009-10
#> 12 2010-02 2010-02        1  1.011018  1.011018 1.011018   2010-02

# All the runs of negative values, as in the run theory with threshold 0
head(index_events(spei12, threshold = 0))
#>     start     end duration     severity   intensity        peak peak.time
#> 1 1980-12 1982-05       18 -20.15861494 -1.11992305 -1.91662561   1981-04
#> 2 1982-10 1983-03        6  -2.63316542 -0.43886090 -0.72854831   1982-11
#> 3 1983-05 1983-06        2  -0.26491019 -0.13245509 -0.18625649   1983-06
#> 4 1984-06 1985-08       15 -10.27038420 -0.68469228 -1.23291130   1985-05
#> 5 1986-03 1986-04        2  -0.08774775 -0.04387387 -0.07104789   1986-04
#> 6 1986-07 1986-07        1  -0.04553927 -0.04553927 -0.04553927   1986-07

# Several series: SPEI-6 and SPEI-12
spei6 <- spei(wichita[, "BAL"], 6, verbose = FALSE)
x <- cbind(spei6 = spei6$fitted, spei12 = spei12$fitted)
index_events(x, min.duration = 3)
